headline: Germany Transforms Coal Mines Into Europe's Largest Wetland
meta_description: Eastern Germany is flooding abandoned lignite mines to create the Lusatian Lakeland, a network of 23 lakes covering 14,000 hectares across Brandenburg and Saxo…
summary_short: Decades of lignite mining left enormous scars across eastern Germany. Now those pits are being reflooded to create a vast new landscape of lakes and wetlands.
body:
Enormous pits carved into eastern Germany's landscape by decades of lignite mining are being transformed into a vast network of lakes and restored land. The Lusatian Lakeland, spanning Brandenburg and Saxony between Berlin and Dresden, comprises 23 post-mining lakes covering about 14,000 hectares of water—making it Europe's largest artificial wetland.

The project works by flooding former open-cast mines and reshaping their surroundings into a cohesive landscape. What was once barren industrial terrain is now becoming a tourist destination, breathing new life into a region scarred by extraction. The transformation shows how careful land restoration can turn environmental damage into ecological opportunity, giving communities both a natural refuge and economic possibility.
quick_facts: 23 lakes created across Brandenburg and Saxony
